The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Let $F:M^m\to N^n$ be smooth and let $Z\subseteq N$ be an embedded submanifold
of codimension $c$, and suppose $F\pitchfork Z$. If $c\le m$, then
$F^{-1}(Z)$ is an embedded submanifold of $M$ of codimension $c$ (possibly empty). If $c>m$,
then $F^{-1}(Z)=\varnothing$. In the first case, for each $p\in F^{-1}(Z)$,

$$ T_pF^{-1}(Z)=\{v\in T_pM:dF_p(v)\in T_{F(p)}Z\}. $$

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

Let $f:M\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, let $p$ be a nondegenerate critical point of
$f$, and let $\lambda$ be the index of $p$. If $n=\dim M$, then there are local
coordinates $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ centered at $p$ in which

$$f=f(p)-\sum_{i=1}^{\lambda}(x^i)^2+\sum_{i=\lambda+1}^{n}(x^i)^2.$$

For $n=0$, both sums are empty.

Let $m\ge 0$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m$ be open around
$(0,0)$, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth with

$$F(0,0)=0,\qquad \frac{\partial F}{\partial u}(0,0)=0,\qquad \frac{\partial^2F}{\partial u^2}(0,0)\ne0.$$

Then, after shrinking $U$, there are a sign $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$, a smooth
function $H$ of the parameter variable, and a smooth local coordinate
change $(u,y)\mapsto (u',y)$ fixing $(0,0)$ such that

$$F(u,y)=H(y)+\varepsilon (u')^2.$$

Use coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$ on Euclidean space-time, with projection $(x,y,z,t)\mapsto(x,y,t)$; $z$ records the crossing order. A local movie move replaces the movies on the two sides of an isolated value $\lambda=0$ in a one-parameter deformation of a projected surface, with the surface and its collars unchanged outside the indicated region. Coordinates and cutoffs are chosen so the two movies have identical boundary frames. The following list specifies the fifteen Carter–Saito types, with their usual numbering. Include both directions, reflections, all compatible strand orientations, and every crossing order allowed by distinct $z$-coordinates. The quadratic and higher-order formulas specify the local topological models; sufficiently small perturbations with the same nonzero derivative signs give the same type.

| Type | Local change of the movie |
|---|---|
| MM1, MM2 | A pair of inverse R1 events is created or removed. In regular-height source coordinates $(v,t)$ the projected curve has local form $(v^2,(t^2-\lambda)v+c v^3)$, $c\ne0$; the two signs of $c$ relative to the quadratic term give the two types. |
| MM3, MM4 | A pair of inverse R2 events is created or removed. After the two projected branches are made graphs, their normal difference is $x^2+t^2-\lambda$ or $x^2-t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM5 | A pair of inverse R3 events is created or removed. With the intersection of two strands continued as the reference point, the signed displacement of the third strand is $t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM6 | An R3 event passes an R2 event: at the projected triple point exactly two projected tangents become parallel, with nonzero quadratic contact and nonzero relative deformation velocity. |
| MM7 | An R2 event meets a branch endpoint of the double-curve locus of an R1 picture. In projected coordinates use $(v^2,tv+\lambda v^3+v^5)$; its double pairs have $r=v^2\ge0$ and $t=-\lambda r-r^2$, so a critical point of the double-curve height enters or leaves through $r=0$. |
| MM8 | A third strand passes the branch point of an R1 picture; superpose a transverse strand on the ordinary cusp unfolding and move its displacement across zero. |
| MM9 | Two R2 critical levels merge and disappear, or are created, at a cubic inflection of the double curve: the branch-difference model is $x^3+\lambda x-t$. |
| MM10 | Four sheets meet at one projected point, with distinct omitted heights. Resolving the quadruple point in the two deformation directions gives the tetrahedral pair of R3 movies. |
| MM11 | A cancelling pair of surface Morse critical points is born or dies. The surface-height model is $u^2+v^3-\lambda v$, allowing both signs of the nondegenerate square and time reversal. |
| MM12 | At an extremum of surface height the projection of its tangent plane has rank one. A local embedded model is $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2+v^2)$; the two movies interchange the extremum with its adjacent R1 picture. |
| MM13 | The corresponding interaction at a saddle, with embedded model $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2-v^2)$. |
| MM14 | A projected strand passes a surface minimum or maximum: superpose an independently displaced regular sheet on the extremum picture. |
| MM15 | The corresponding projected strand passage across a saddle band. |

A **distant interchange** exchanges the order of two elementary movie events with disjoint spatial supports, including Reidemeister events and Morse events; it is not restricted to two critical points of the smooth surface-height function. A planar isotopy of a whole movie and the insertion or removal of stationary frames do not count as additional local types. Sweep-around is a separate spherical operation, absent from this Euclidean list.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume countable choice. Let $K_0,K_1\subset S^3$ be smooth oriented knots. A smooth oriented knot cobordism from $K_0$ to $K_1$ is a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ whose boundary is $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$, with product collars at both ends. A **generic movie** for $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing a generic projection of the slices $S^3\times\{t\}$ to the plane and a Morse height function on $\Sigma$, then recording the oriented link diagram at each regular level. Intermediate regular levels may be links with any finite number of components. After choosing the projection and height generically, the finitely many exceptional levels are isolated and distinct: between them the diagrams change by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move, and at them the surface height has one nondegenerate minimum (a birth), one nondegenerate maximum (a death), or one index-one critical point (a saddle band move). A movie includes its ordered list of frames and these elementary changes; no claim that two movies of the same cobordism are equivalent is part of this definition.

Assume countable choice. Fix $\infty\in S^3$, put $A=\{\infty\}\times[0,1]$, and identify its complement with $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$. Let $S_0,S_1$ be compact smooth oriented link cobordisms disjoint from $A$, with the same fixed boundary parametrizations and product collars. If they are ambient isotopic in $S^3\times[0,1]$ relative to those collars, then their comparison factors into finitely many ambient isotopies supported in the Euclidean complement and finitely many local sheet passages through $A$. Each sheet passage occurs at a regular surface-height point and gives the sweep-around move: in planar movies, a closing arc for a one-interval tangle travels over the tangle to the opposite side and returns underneath, or the inverse, retaining its orientation. All end collars remain fixed. No assertion that a sweep-around is generated by the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito moves, or that any homology map respects it, is made.

Assume countable choice. Let two finite generic planar movies represent compact smooth oriented surfaces in $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$, with the same parametrized boundary and product collars. If their embedded surfaces are ambient isotopic with compact support relative to those collars, then the two movies are related by a finite sequence of the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito local types, distant interchanges of disjoint elementary movie events, and planar isotopies. All orientations and omitted-coordinate crossing orders are retained. This statement concerns Euclidean isotopies; it supplies no sweep-around relation.
